tasks.title: Fix parse_duration: minutes use wrong seconds multiplier

declaration.objective: parse_duration converts minutes correctly and remains correct for hours/seconds and invalid input, with regression tests

criteria.statement: Hours-only and seconds-only durations keep working
Invalid input still rejected with InvalidDuration; grammar in durations/parse.py unchanged
Regression tests covering minutes are added

execution_fit.choice: FIT: one-line fix to the minutes multiplier plus regression tests, verifiable via pytest
execution_fit.rationale: criteria: all four are concrete and testable via parse_duration's return values and pytest.raises; capability: root cause is a single wrong constant (_UNIT_SECONDS['m']=3600 instead of 60) in durations/parse.py, fix is trivial and does not touch the grammar/regex; hardest: making sure the fix doesn't disturb the existing invalid-input rejection tests or the parsing order logic; evidence: run pytest on tests/test_parse.py plus new minute cases, and manually eval parse_duration on the three example strings from the issue; not authorised/equipped: will not commit, push, merge, or run tallyback land/settle beyond what this task asks; stop if: pytest fails after the fix or any existing test regresses

claims.statement: Fixed the minutes multiplier in durations/parse.py (_UNIT_SECONDS['m'] 3600 -> 60), leaving the grammar (_PART regex, _ORDER, control flow) unchanged. Added regression tests for 30m, 1h30m, and 2h15m30s. Full pytest suite (14 tests, including all 8 invalid-input cases) passes.

evidence.note: 14 passed, 0 failed: test_hours, test_seconds, test_hours_and_seconds, new test_minutes (30m->1800), test_hours_and_minutes (1h30m->5400), test_hours_minutes_and_seconds (2h15m30s->8130), and all 8 test_rejects_invalid parametrizations. Fix: durations/parse.py _UNIT_SECONDS['m'] changed from 3600 to 60; regex/_PART, _ORDER, and control flow unchanged (confirmed via git diff, one-line change).

confidence.rationale: Full pytest run (14/14 passed) plus direct interpreter checks of the three issue examples and a git diff review confirming the grammar file's regex/order/control-flow are unchanged; only the wrong _UNIT_SECONDS['m'] constant was corrected.

settlement.rationale: All four declared acceptance criteria are supported with high confidence: minutes now convert correctly (30m->1800, 1h30m->5400, 2h15m30s->8130), hours-only/seconds-only durations still work, invalid input is still rejected with the grammar file's regex/order/control-flow unchanged, and regression tests were added. The change itself has not been committed to Git, so this accepts the work product without authorizing landing/merge.
